    if tab.is_active then
      background = '#2b2042'
      foreground = '#c0c0c0'
    elseif hover then
      background = '#3b3052'
      foreground = '#909090'
    end

    local edge_foreground = background

    local title = tab_title(tab)

    -- ensure that the titles fit in the available space,
    -- and that we have room for the edges.
    title = wezterm.truncate_right(title, max_width - 2)

    return {
      { Background = { Color = edge_background } },
      { Foreground = { Color = edge_foreground } },
      { Text = SOLID_LEFT_ARROW },
      { Background = { Color = background } },
      { Foreground = { Color = foreground } },
      { Text = title },
      { Background = { Color = edge_background } },
      { Foreground = { Color = edge_foreground } },
      { Text = SOLID_RIGHT_ARROW },
    }
  end
)

Asked claude how to make the drawing characters thicker because I want: Yes! There are a few ways to make line-drawing (box-drawing) characters thicker in WezTerm, depending on what exactly you're after:

---

### 1. `underline_thickness` (primary option)

The `underline_thickness` setting overrides the base thickness of underlines, and it's also used for rendering split pane dividers and a number of other lines in custom glyphs. So bumping it up will make box-drawing lines thicker too.

```lua
config.underline_thickness = "200%"  -- doubles the default thickness
-- or use pixel values:
config.underline_thickness = 2
```

The caveat, as noted in a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/issues/4610), is that changing `underline_thickness` also modifies how box-drawing characters and other custom glyphs are drawn, so there's currently no way to make underlines thicker without also making those glyphs thicker — they're coupled together.

---

### 2. `custom_block_glyphs` + `anti_alias_custom_block_glyphs`

WezTerm renders many box/block characters itself rather than from the font. You can tweak this behavior:

```lua
config.custom_block_glyphs = true          -- WezTerm draws the glyphs (default)
config.anti_alias_custom_block_glyphs = true
```

Setting `custom_block_glyphs = false` causes border symbols to be rendered as bold (matching how other terminals like Alacritty render them), but it can break some other symbols. Worth trying if you want bolder-looking lines.

---

### 3. `freetype_render_target` for overall stroke weight

Switching to `freetype_render_target = "HorizontalLcd"` gives thicker-looking strokes overall.

```lua
config.freetype_render_target = "HorizontalLcd"
```

---

### Putting it together

A reasonable starting config to experiment with:

```lua
config.underline_thickness = "200%"
config.custom_block_glyphs = true
config.anti_alias_custom_block_glyphs = true
config.freetype_render_target = "HorizontalLcd"
```

The `underline_thickness` option is the most direct lever for line-drawing character weight, but do be aware it also affects underlines everywhere.
